item.title: Booking can compel staff to spend two days in the office: court
item.description:
Booking can compel staff to spend two days in the office: court

October 28, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

A court has ruled that travel website Booking.com can compel its staff to spend at least two days a week in the office, settling a dispute with the company’s works council.

The decision was widely expected after the judge remarked at an earlier hearing that requiring employees to spend 40% of their contracted hours on site was “very normal”.

Just over a quarter of Booking.com’s 7,000 staff currently travel to its head office in Amsterdam twice a week. The company had advised its workers to spend two days in the office to promote better workplace relations, training and efficient working practices.

But when bosses tried to make the two-day guideline a mandatory requirement, the works council objected. It said the impact on people’s work-life balance, commuting times and travel costs was too great and questioned whether it would lead to improved performance.

The judge said the company had taken employees’ concerns into account and responded by introducing a six-month transition period and deciding to set the minimum office time at 40% rather than 50% or 60%.

Booking said it welcomed the judgment, pointing out that the two-day rule was not a new measure but a “strengthening of our current policy”.

“We value the relationship with our works council and will continue to hold constructive dialogue with them and our employees as we roll this policy out further,” a spokesman said.

Employment lawyer Pascal Besselink told RTL Nieuws other companies that wanted staff to spend more time in the office would be studying the judgment closely.

“They will always strive to maintain a good relationship with their employees and works council and consult thoroughly on arrangements about home working,” he said.

item.title: WWII explosives found at Eindhoven airport
item.description:
WWII explosives found at Eindhoven airport

October 28, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Two explosives from the Second World War have been discovered at Eindhoven Airport during renovation groundwork next to one of the airport’s runways.

A spokesperson for the Royal Marechaussee, a branch of the military police, said the explosives were found on Wednesday morning on the military side of the airport, which shares the runway with civilian planes, Brabants Dagblad reported.

One of the items is a mortar shell, and the other has not yet been identified, the spokesperson told broadcaster NOS.

No air traffic was disrupted by the discovery and no civilians were at any harm.

item.title: “Strict” Dutch border controls lead to 650 refusals in 21 months
item.description:
“Strict” Dutch border controls lead to 650 refusals in 21 months

October 28, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Fewer than 700 people were turned away at the Dutch border in 21 months of extra border controls that were introduced as part of the “strictest asylum policy ever”.

Border police stopped 43,210 vehicles and checked 182,700 people crossing land borders into Belgium and Germany after the last government reintroduced border controls in December 2024.

A total of 650 people were refused entry while trying to cross the border by road during the period until the checks, introduced by former asylum minister Marjolein Faber of the far-right PVV party, ended in September.

Police arrested 300 people, of whom 40 were suspected of involvement in human trafficking. The government also said 140 people claimed asylum after being stopped at the border.

Some 70% of people stopped at the land borders were EU citizens, asylum minister Bart van den Brink said in a letter to parliament. Border police also checked 398,000 people travelling on flights within the Schengen zone, 85% of whom had EU passports.

Van den Brink said the checks were stepped up to deal with the “significant impact of the continued influx of irregular migration”.

According to Frontex figures, the number of irregular border crossings is down by 26% since 2024. In the same period there has been a 25% drop in first-time asylum applications in the Netherlands.

Schengen zone rules allow member states to reinstate border checks as a temporary measure if there is a threat to security or public order, but they must keep the EU updated on progress.

item.title: Police seize dozens of servers in Limburg over cybercrime
item.description:
Police seize dozens of servers in Limburg over cybercrime

October 28, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The police have seized dozens of servers from a data centre in Limburg that were allegedly used to distribute child pornography, as well as carry out cyberattacks and phishing scams.

The seizures are part of an investigation into an unnamed company, a so-called bulletproof hoster, which provides web space and server access to criminal groups.

Police say they have now gained information on over 3,000 customers who used the servers, and that the hunt for those people is now underway.

At the same time, the FBI and German police also acted against suspects revealed in the investigation, seizing cryptocurrency and shutting down online infrastructure.

The location of the data centre has not yet been made public since the servers in question were housed alongside legal ones, local broadcaster L1 reported.

Police confirmed around 50 servers were taken on Tuesday. The US department of justice announced at the same time that the FBI had taken action against a site called Virtualine, with assistance from Dutch, British and German authorities. The connection between these cases has not yet been confirmed.

The seizure follows a raid in July on the hosting company used by Motherless, a porn website which contained huge amounts of abusive material. NOS later reported that the site’s own employees had uploaded child pornography.

item.title: Free as a bird? New law for freelancers goes into consultation
item.description:
Partner content

Free as a bird? New law for freelancers goes into consultation

October 28, 2026

If you work as a freelancer or have your own business, you should be aware of a new law that the Dutch government has just proposed.

The Zelfstandigenwet, or freelance law, aims to create more “peace and clarity” for people who want to work on their own, according to employment minister Thierry Aartsen.

There has already been an exodus of freelancers due to a crackdown on “sham” self-employment, but tax advisers believe people should not panic.

“Don’t get scared,” said an adviser for Blue Umbrella tax service. “Believe in your business, believe in being self-supporting and go for it! Economic growth comes from small and medium-sized enterprises and the government knows that.”

Tests
The new law proposal, which could come into force in 2028 if the minority government manages to find support, will make it clearer what you need to do to be considered a freelancer, or “zzp’er”.

In the past, this group could get a special document from the tax office confirming their freelance status but instead of this formal recognition, there will be a series of tests.

You will need to be registered with the Chamber of Commerce (Kamer van Koophandel) – which is true for most businesses, in any case. You will also need a VAT number and a business bank account, and you must have worked for at least three different clients in two years. Freelancers may also need a specific financial buffer, insurance and pension savings.

Another test will examine how independently you work, including whether you can organise your working hours and take financial risks.

Portfolio
Blue Umbrella recommends making it clear to your potential customers that you will meet the requirements. “Make a portfolio of your clients and what you did in the past year,” the advisor said. “Show that you have a substantial business with multiple clients and you are developing yourself. That gives them trust that they can hire you.”

There is currently an internet consultation running for all freelancers and interested parties until October 29. When the law comes in, however, it may be tested in court: it is not clear why someone with three clients could objectively be called freelance as opposed to someone with two.

Reduction
Under pressure from unions and the European Commission, which has linked some of the compensation for the Netherlands during corona to reducing “fake freelancing”, the number of Dutch self-employed workers has already gone down.

A report last week from the DNB central bank found that there were 131,000 fewer freelancers halfway through 2026 than there were at the end of 2024. The peak came in 2024, when almost 1.3 million people worked for themselves.

According to the report, a third of those who stopped found a permanent job or one that could become a fixed contract. But 40% of the people who stopped freelancing switched to work in a completely different occupation, and 7% became unemployed.

Complex
Blue Umbrella has seen some clients close their businesses too, but stressed that people should not despair: this issue has been around for a long time and, in practice, it is complex. The proposed law aims to help people prove they are genuinely self-employed in future but it would not necessarily stop people who are currently freelancing, under the current rules.

“If you talk about whether someone can make their own decisions as one of the factors to judge whether they are self-employed, it’s a hard question,” said the adviser. “Even as a contractor, you always follow the instructions of the client. You can’t just do your own thing because you think it’s your decision. That would be absurd!”

That said, it’s a good idea to be careful with your finances and consider what extra investments you might want to make, if there are uncertainties in the future of self-employment in the Netherlands.

But do not give up! “The biggest tax revenue comes from small businesses and they are our economic drivers, not the big companies,” he said. “The world will change, and at the end of the day, you have to do it yourself, not rely on the government!”

Find out more about Blue Umbrella’s cost-efficient scheme for businesses and tax services for internationals

item.title: PostNL worker faces 10 years over deadly fake pill webshop
item.description:
PostNL worker faces 10 years over deadly fake pill webshop

October 28, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The public prosecution service (OM) is demanding prison sentences of 10 and 6.5 years for two suspects accused of involvement in a counterfeit medicine webshop, whose products appear to have led to the deaths of three people.

The pair are alleged to have worked for an organisation that set up dozens of online sites offering prescription pills like sedatives, painkillers and sleeping aids. The sites were shutdown last week and three people arrested for orchestrating the operation.

People bought the pills online without knowing what was actually in them. Some contained powerful synthetic opioids like nitazenes, which can be far more deadly than fentanyl.

The two suspects were not the main players in the case; one is accused of storing and packing the orders, and the other of using his role in the postal service to ensure deliveries were made.

The PostNL employee is also suspected of importing and dealing in large quantities of cocaine, according to broadcaster NOS.

Both suspects say they had no idea they were helping distribute contaminated pills. A lawyer for one of the defendants described his client as a “glorified assembly-line worker”.

item.title: King sees challenges and successes on visit to asylum centre
item.description:
King sees challenges and successes on visit to asylum centre

October 28, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

King Willem-Alexander has visited one of the Netherlands’ longest running accommodation centres for asylum seekers to talk to refugees and local residents.

The king received an enthusiastic reception from the 530 people living in the centre in Leersum, Utrecht province, which has been operational for 35 years.

He said he wanted to see how a refugee centre “can be integrated into a local community”, but also gain an insight into the challenges for people living in the area.

During his visit he was shown the facilities in the centre such as a women’s café with yoga and cooking workshops, a bicycle repair shop and support for refugees looking for work or training.

“We all know what the problems are and we see them a lot,” the king said. “But it is also good to be able to show, by being here and bringing lots of journalists along, that things can go very well.”

He was handed a bundle of letters from primary school children, in which they told their personal stories and described how they missed their parents.

The head of the school, Bea, who has been teaching refugee children for 16 years, told AD.nl that the outlook was bleaker than at any time she could remember because of the length of time it is taking for asylum claims to be processed.

“A large group of children are still waiting for their parents, whom they haven’t seen for two or three years in some cases, to be given residency permits,” she said. “We have to deal with that as well as teaching classes.”

item.title: Animal rights party renews bill to ban cruel slaughter methods
item.description:
Animal rights party renews bill to ban cruel slaughter methods

October 28, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The animals rights party PvdD is making a renewed effort to pass a bill that would ban a number of common and cruel livestock slaughter methods, such as electric waterbathing, gassing via CO2, and all non-stun methods.

The bill, sent to MPs today, was first submitted in 2025, and would also ban selling cows, pigs and horses for slaughter while they’re in the last third of a pregnancy. Tipping poultry out of crates while they’re still conscious (a common practice) would also be outlawed.

According to agriculture ministry figures for 2024, 25,895 animals – cattle, calves, sheep and goats – were slaughtered without stunning under religious rites.

In the same figures, some 10.5 million pigs were slaughtered at abattoirs that use CO2 gassing, while more than 62.7 million broiler chickens, 4.6 million ducks and nearly 4,000 turkeys were killed at slaughterhouses that use electric waterbaths.

PvdD MP Esther Ouwehand, who drafted the bill, told broadcaster NOS: “the aim of the law is to limit the suffering of animals during slaughter as much as possible.”

The party first began trying to outlaw non-stun slaughter in 2008 but was voted down in the Senate over freedom of religion concerns. But the Council of State said last year a ban would not necessarily breach freedom religion following European court rulings on bans in Belgium.

item.title: Zelenskyy visits The Hague as Dutch announce €1.2bn aid package
item.description:
Zelenskyy visits The Hague as Dutch announce €1.2bn aid package

October 28, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy will meet prime minister Rob Jetten in The Hague on Wednesday on his first visit to the Netherlands since Jetten’s centre-right coalition gained power in February.

Zelenskyy will hold a press conference in the Catshuis, the prime minister’s official residence, after talking to Jetten, defence minister Dilan Yesilgöz and foreign affairs minister Tom Berendsen.

Later in the day he will attend a reception with king Willem-Alexander in Huis ten Bosch, the monarch’s residential palace in The Hague.

The Dutch government also announced it would be spending €40 million to help repair Ukrainian energy facilities that have been damaged by Russian military strikes aimed at cutting off supplies during the winter.

The investment, announced by foreign trade minister Sjoerd Sjoerdsma during a visit to Kyiv, is part of a €1.2 billion package of non-military aid for the next three years.

“It is very important for the safety of us all to keep supporting Ukraine so that they can keep up the fight,” Sjoerdsma said.

The cabinet is also buying €55 million worth of components such as generators, transformers and compressors from Dutch companies to send to Ukraine.

A total of €136 million has been made available and the government has increased its export credit insurance to reduce the risk to companies that send equipment to the war zone.

Spring visit

Jetten first met Zelenskyy as prime minister on a visit to Kyiv in March, two weeks after his cabinet was sworn in. The Ukrainian president said the hastily arranged trip showed his country remained a “priority” for the Dutch government.

Zelenskyy was last in the Netherlands in December, when he had lunch with the outgoing prime minister Dick Schoof and addressed both houses of parliament.

It was his fourth speech to Dutch legislators since the full-scale Russian invasion began in February 2022.

The visit marked the launch of a claims commission backed by 30 countries, which will assess war-related damage in Ukraine and arrange to pay compensation from a dedicated fund.

item.title: Search for missing kite surfer stood down after board found
item.description:
Search for missing kite surfer stood down after board found

October 28, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

A search for an 18-year-old kite surfer who went missing during Storm Boelo has been called off after his kite and board washed up on the shore on Scheveningen.

The family of the man said they were “preparing for the worst” after police said there was only a small chance he was still alive.

The man was reported missing at around 2pm on Sunday, as gale force winds and high waves battered the Dutch coast. A lifeboat and helicopter searched the waters, but rescue efforts were hampered by the weather.

The search around the Zuidelijk Havenhoofd was stood down at around midday on Tuesday after the man’s board was recovered.

A spokesman for media liaison organisation Namens de Familie said his the man’s family were “grateful for all support from everyone” and had not given up hope.
